1.why: Reset records store an identityScope hash and /api/new-password requires session.resetVerified plus session.recoveryIdentity, but /api/verify-reset accepts any valid code from any session and simply adopts the token's scope rather than comparing it to a user the requester claims, and only one mock account exists.

2.why: Codes are bound to a hashed identity scope, marked used on first verification, and expire after 10 minutes, so a given code cannot be replayed against a different account (and the mock has only one account).

3.why: After /api/new-password the loop over all sessions clears authenticated, pendingMfa, privacyAccepted and appointmentBooked, so pre-reset sessions no longer work.

4.why: The app serves over TLS with cert/key files, redirects HTTP to HTTPS with 308, and sets HSTS, but no minimum/latest TLS version is explicitly configured (relies on Bun defaults).

5.why: Reset codes are 32 random bytes stored only as SHA-256 hashes and passwords use bcrypt (cost 10), which is appropriate, though no data-at-rest encryption exists (in-memory Maps only).

6.why: There is no email delivery at all; instead the raw reset code is returned in the JSON response and printed into the visible 'Logs' pane and console, so the simulated delivery does not guard the secret.

7.why: Inputs are type/length checked, identifiers normalized, reset codes matched against a strict /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{32,128}$/ allowlist, passwords policy-validated, and all UI text is written via textContent.

8.why: The only redirect is a fixed 308 to https://localhost + internal path (Host header never used), and client navigation uses hard-coded internal routes from an allowlisted set.

9.why: No email templates exist in the code, and the substitute simulated log/message output is inserted with textContent under a nonce-based CSP, so no user HTML or script can appear.

10.why: Error responses are generic with no stack traces, but the reset code and the MFA code ('246810') are deliberately written to console.log and to the on-page Logs element.

11.why: The initial account password 'Initial!DemoPassword2025', the static MFA code '246810', and the valid recovery identity are all hard-coded literals in the source, even though the password is hashed with bcrypt in memory.

12.why: A hard-coded default credential ('Initial!DemoPassword2025' plus fixed MFA code 246810) is provisioned at startup and can be used to sign in without any forced change.

13.why: Account-scoped lockout after 5 failed logins and 5 failed MFA attempts (5-minute lock), plus 3/10min recovery-request and 5/10min code-verification throttles, all server-side and session-independent.

14.why: Although the message text is identical, only the valid recovery identity gets a response containing a 'code' field (and the UI then renders a verification link), so the response clearly distinguishes existing from non-existing accounts.

15.why: Codes come from crypto.getRandomValues (32 bytes, base64url), are stored hashed with an identity scope, are single-use and expire in 10 minutes.
